saturation_note: Saturation hit after the 'E Ink Marquee' query. Seven consecutive searches from deliberately different angles (outdoor platform, ESL-new-entrant, price comparison, module houses, non-Asian geography, 2026 launches, large-format supplier lists) returned either zero new names or only unverifiable Alibaba-tier OEM names from an AI aggregator page. The one exception was the museum/gallery query, which found Artec Design - that was a use-case-specific lane, not the retail/ESL lane, and it confirms that the productive remaining direction is application verticals (museum, transit, healthcare) rather than more retail vendors. The structural finding is that the ePaper Industry Alliance member database (150-260+ members) is the real backstop against this sampling gap; I enumerated its visible members but the full database is behind registration. COUNTING BASIS: new_vendor_count = 28 = every entry in the vendors[] array, all of which are absent from the supplied known list. known_vendor_count = 9 = known-list vendors re-encountered during this sweep (E Ink Holdings, PPDS/Philips Tableaux, Visionect, Geniatech, Samsung, SEEKINK, Dalian Good Display, Papercast, Digital View); MEiNK never appeared in any result. One caution on the new count: MyGica publishes model numbers identical to Geniatech's, so it is Geniatech's brand and is deliberately NOT counted as a new vendor - a naive sweep would have double-counted it. Three of the 28 (Wallboard, SyncSign, ePaper Industry Alliance) are a CMS vendor, a sub-13-inch hardware vendor and a trade body respectively rather than large-format display vendors; excluding those gives 25 genuinely new large-format display vendors.

leads_not_followed.lead: The full ePaper Industry Alliance member database at epaperia.org/Search.html and the per-member pages at /Members/[ID].html. EPIA claims 150-260+ members; roughly 50 were visible to me without registration.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: This is the single highest-leverage remaining action and the structural fix for the sampling gap the brief describes. A registered account would enumerate the whole industry in one pass instead of vendor-by-vendor searching. Their 'ePaper Mall' also publishes actual prices, which almost no vendor does.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether Advantech's DeviceOn/ePaper exposes a scriptable REST API for pushing an image to a specific display. Their ESS-WIKI documentation host (ess-wiki.advantech.com.tw) did not resolve for me.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: Advantech is the best overall candidate found - 28.6 inch Spectra 6 at 3060x2160, USB and Ethernet, and a management server that installs on your own Ubuntu box. The only missing fact is whether the archive could script image pushes rather than clicking through a web UI. That one answer would likely settle the whole search.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether the LG 32-inch e-paper display accepts USB media or local-network content directly through webOS, without SuperSign.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: A tier-1 manufacturer, 32 inch, QHD, colour, battery-powered. LG's webOS signage line has historically supported USB playback. If that carries over, this becomes a mainstream, well-supported, no-cloud option - the most durable of any candidate here.

leads_not_followed.lead: AUO Display Plus's aecoPost integration model. Their product page 404'd; AUO Display Plus exists specifically to sell finished units to integrators and end customers.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: 31.5 inch Spectra 6 at 2560x1440 is arguably the best artwork panel found, from a tier-1 manufacturer with an integrator-friendly sales posture. Only the content-delivery mechanism is unknown.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether TintTech or Artec Design plan a colour (Spectra 6) panel, or would build one on commission.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: They already have the hard part - a self-hosted Debian CMS with a REST API, a perpetual licence and no cloud. Their only disqualifier is that every panel they sell is greyscale. A colour variant would make them the outright best fit for this use case.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether the Agile ACE 'open integration standard' has, or will have, a self-hostable reference implementation or published interface specification.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: ACE is the only attempt in this industry to standardise the CMS-to-e-paper interface. Today it is cloud-only, which blocks self-hosting. If it opens up it would unlock the largest panels in the segment (75 inch) and many vendors at once.

leads_not_followed.lead: Sharp's EP-C251 full datasheet - specifically whether the PC connection is a scriptable interface or a manual desktop utility. Sharp's global and NEC-branded e-paper pages both 404'd or redirected away.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: USB-C thumbdrive loading on a 25.3 inch colour panel from a tier-1 manufacturer is the single most promising local-push signal found. Whether it can be automated determines if it suits a self-hosted archive app or only manual curation.

Listed for completeness; would need first-party verification before being treated as real.
